title: Kentucky defeats No. 9 Texas A&M 31-21, first victory over Aggies since 1953
dek: Kentucky, a 13.5-point to 16.5-point underdog, defeated No. 9 Texas A&M 31-21 on the road on September 19. The Wildcats trailed 7-0 before scoring 28 consecutive points and controlling the second and third quarters. The victory marks the program's first win over Texas A&M in 73 years and the first marquee win for first-year coach Will Stein.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Kentucky defeated No. 9 Texas A&M 31-21 after trailing 7-0, marking the program's first victory over the Aggies since 1953 and the first marquee win for first-year coach Will Stein.
bottom_line: Major college football upset in Week 3; ranked team defeated on the road with playoff implications.
body: Kentucky defeated No. 9 Texas A&M 31-21 on the road in College Station on September 19, in one of the season's most significant upsets. According to CBS Sports, the Wildcats entered as 16.5-point underdogs, though Sporting News reported the spread at 13.5 points. The game was played in front of 105,186 fans at Kyle Field.

The result marks Kentucky's first victory over Texas A&M since 1953 and the first marquee win for first-year coach Will Stein, who at 36 is the youngest head coach in the SEC. Stein was formerly Oregon's offensive coordinator before taking the Kentucky job.

Kentucky trailed 7-0 early before rattling off 28 consecutive points, per CBS Sports. The Wildcats took a 28-7 lead midway through the third quarter after Texas A&M failed to convert on a fourth-and-2 from its own 33-yard line. Quarterback Marcel Reed missed open running back Carsyn Baker in the flat on that play, according to CBS Sports, returning possession to Kentucky in prime field position.

Kentucky's offense executed three 75-yard-or-longer touchdown drives in the second and third quarters, per CBS Sports. Running backs CJ Baxter and Jason Patterson led the attack. Quarterback Kenny Minchey completed 11 straight passes across both halves and threw a 42-yard touchdown strike to freshman Kenny Darby to open third-quarter scoring, per CBS Sports. After Texas A&M cut the lead to 28-14 early in the fourth quarter, offensive coordinator Joe Sloan called a play-action pass on second-and-8 that Minchey converted into a 32-yard completion to tight end Henry Boyer, according to CBS Sports. A 52-yard field goal by Adam Zouagui extended the lead to 31-14.

Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed was intercepted twice by Kentucky defenders. According to CBS Sports, Reed threw a baffling interception in Kentucky territory late in the first quarter and was intercepted again on a bad overthrow with 6:34 remaining. Sporting News reported that Sam Greene intercepted Reed during the first half and Jordan Castell added an interception during the fourth quarter. Reed did throw a 5-yard touchdown run and later connected with Micah Riley for a 5-yard touchdown that cut Kentucky's lead to 31-21.

The context surrounding this upset centers on Kentucky's collapse the previous week. The Wildcats led Alabama 17-13 at halftime before being outscored 32-0 in the second half, losing 45-17. Texas A&M had dominated its first two opponents, beating Missouri State 50-0 and Arizona State 48-20, per Sporting News. The Aggies mounted a 30-3 comeback against South Carolina a year ago, so the script appeared set for another late-game rally.
Kentucky improved to 2-1 with the victory, while Texas A&M fell to 2-1. Jay Bateman, who was Texas A&M's defensive coordinator in 2024 and 2025, is now on Kentucky's staff under Stein.

The Bottom Line: Kentucky's second-half mastery against a top-10 team on the road suggests the Stein regime can sustain execution under pressure, though the Wildcats' 32-point collapse at Alabama the prior week remains unresolved. Texas A&M's ranking and playoff position will face recalibration, and whether the Aggies can recover from this road loss against future opponents will determine if this proves a season-altering setback.
